policy: This triage records only visible morphology in the frozen secondary locator crops from voynich.nu. It may prioritize primary-image review but MUST NOT set primary_image_verified=true, freeze a before->after transcription, assign HIGH confidence, or include an event in the confirmatory test.

source.note: The page explicitly lists these twelve apparent emendation crops; the page itself states that such cases are few and minor.

candidates.visible_morphology: A locally darkened complex tall glyph with overlapping strokes is visible near the crop centre; the underlying earlier state is not uniquely separable in the locator crop.

A compact central glyph contains several superposed dark strokes. Independent discussion proposes incompatible readings of what lies underneath, so the pre-state is not recoverable from the crop alone.
The candidate region contains a discrete local stroke anomaly rather than a fully opaque blot; individual stroke boundaries remain partially visible in the locator crop.
A localized glyph in the running word shows visibly superposed/darkened strokes while surrounding glyphs remain legible.
The event is dominated by a dense dark blob/overwrite; the lower-layer stroke topology is not visually separable in this crop.
A tall glyph has closely spaced/doubled vertical strokes and local darkening, with adjacent glyphs remaining clear.
A short word contains one conspicuously darkened local glyph; the crop does not by itself reveal a unique erased or overwritten predecessor.
A tall double-stem glyph is much darker than neighbouring strokes. Because page-wide re-inking has been raised independently for f79r, morphology alone cannot distinguish correction from retouching.
A localized complex glyph in the word shows darker superposed strokes but not a completely opaque blot.
The candidate position is a dense dark loop/blob with little separable lower-layer structure in the locator crop.
The candidate strokes are faint and low-contrast, with no uniquely identifiable earlier form visible in the locator crop.
A tall glyph contains paired/darkened vertical strokes while the rest of the word is comparatively clean; retouch versus content-changing addition is unresolved.
